jingle-in-july.title: Jingle in July 2026
jingle-in-july.intro: An Ugly Holiday Sweater Fashion Show Benefiting CORE.
jingle-in-july.detail: The July 8, 2026 event at The Beverly Theater combined Scholar-designed holiday fashion, community celebration, sponsorship, and fundraising for CORE programs.

sections.heading: Holiday cheer. Summer style. Student impact.
body: The source event page described a retro-inspired summer holiday celebration featuring an ugly sweater runway show designed by Scholars, cocktails and refreshments, music, community supporters, and opportunities to give.

sections.heading: Event details
body: The Beverly Theater, 515 S. Sixth Street, Las Vegas, NV 89101

sections.heading: Why it mattered
body: The event was positioned as a fundraiser supporting educational access, mentorship, workforce readiness, and opportunity for students and families throughout Southern Nevada.

news.title: News & stories
news.intro: Read recent source-site stories about access, voice, opportunity, and educational equity.
news.detail: The demo brings the three most recent stories into the SPA so visitors can discover them without leaving the main experience.

who-gets-a-microphone.title: Who Gets A Microphone
who-gets-a-microphone.intro: A small Las Vegas stage became a reminder that access to expression, encouragement, and an audience is part of equity too.
who-gets-a-microphone.detail: The source story reflects on a karaoke fundraiser and asks who gets encouraged to perform, who gets access to lessons and training, and who learns that their voice matters.

sections.heading: Voice is an opportunity
body: The article connects educational equity with less obvious forms of access: music programs, creative outlets, performance opportunities, encouragement, and the confidence to take up space.

sections.heading: Why it belongs in the CORE story
body: CORE’s broader work is not only about academics; it is also about helping young people see possibility, practice confidence, and connect with people and experiences that broaden what feels available to them.

who-gets-access-first.title: Who Gets Access First?
who-gets-access-first.intro: Two students can sit in the same classroom and have very different access to opportunity.
who-gets-access-first.detail: The source article argues that equity is not only about resources; it is also about access to information, mentorship, real-world experiences, and networks that open doors.

sections.heading: Access turns potential into direction
body: Some students grow up knowing what careers exist, how to pursue them, and people who have done it before. Others may be equally capable but missing that map.

sections.heading: How CORE shows up
body: The article points to speed mentoring, career exploration, and Parent Academy workshops as ways CORE connects students and families with people and perspectives that help make opportunity visible.

equity-at-the-holidays.title: Equity at the Holidays
equity-at-the-holidays.intro: Holiday breaks can reveal differences in what students can access outside the classroom.
equity-at-the-holidays.detail: The source story focuses on middle-grade students and the uneven access to reliable internet, quiet study spaces, healthy meals, enrichment, and emotional stability during school breaks.

sections.heading: Why the break matters
body: Middle school is a pivotal time for identity, independence, and academic growth. The article argues that for under-resourced families, a holiday break may be destabilizing rather than restorative.

sections.heading: Equity between semesters
body: The story uses the holiday period to show why educational equity depends on support beyond classroom instruction alone.
